'''Pomonok''' is a [[working class]] neighborhood within the [[Flushing, Queens|Flushing]] area in the [[New York City]] [[Boroughs of New York City|borough]] of [[Queens]]. Its borders are the [[Interstate 495 (New York)|Long Island Expressway]] to the north; [[Kissena Boulevard]] to the west; 73rd Avenue to the south; and 164th Street to the east. The surrounding neighborhoods are [[Queensboro Hill, Queens|Queensboro Hill]] to the north; [[Auburndale, Queens|Auburndale]] to the northeast; [[Kew Gardens Hills, Queens|Kew Gardens Hills]] to the west; and the [[Utopia, Queens|Utopia]]/[[Hillcrest, Queens|Hillcrest]] areas of [[Fresh Meadows, Queens|Fresh Meadows]] to both the east and southeast.

The neighborhood is notably home to two large housing developments, both of which are along Jewel Avenue. Those developments being the Pomonok Houses, maintained by the [[New York City Housing Authority]] between Kissena and Parsons Boulevards <ref>[http://www.nyc.gov/html/nycha/html/developments/queenspomonok.shtml NYCHA] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090823024751/http://www.nyc.gov/html/nycha/html/developments/queenspomonok.shtml|date=2009-08-23}} Pomonok Houses</ref> and the Electchester [[Housing cooperative|co-op]] between Parsons Boulevard and 164th Street. Both developments were built between 1949 and 1951 on the site of the former [[Pomonok Country Club]].

The neighborhood’s name comes from the [[Algonquian languages|Algonquian]] name for [[Long Island]],<ref>{{citation |last=Bright |first=William |title=Native American Placenames of the United States |page=373 |year=2004 |url=https://archive.org/details/nativeamericanpl0000brig/page/372/mode/2up}}</ref> and means either "land of tribute" or "land where there is travelling by water".<ref>{{cite book |last1=Jackson |first1=Kenneth T. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=lI5ERUmHf3YC&dq=pomonok+queens+land+of+tribute&pg=PT4743 |title=The Encyclopedia of New York City: Second Edition |last2=Keller |first2=Lisa |last3=Flood |first3=Nancy |date=December 2010 |publisher=Yale University Press |isbn=978-0-300-18257-6}}</ref>[[File:Ibewbuilding.jpg|thumb|300px|The Electchester Local 3 Union Building in October 2007]]Pomonok is part of [[Queens Community Board 8|Queens Community District 8]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Queens Community Board 8 |url=http://www.queenscb8.org/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070928103915/http://www.queenscb8.org/ |archive-date=September 28, 2007 |access-date=September 25, 2014}}</ref> and is also patrolled by the 107th Precinct of the [[New York City Police Department]].{{maplink|frame=y|frame-align=right|zoom=13|type=shape|from=Neighbourhoods/New York City/Pomonok.map|text=Map of Pomonok}}

== History ==

The [[Pomonok Country Club]] was a [[golf course]] in Pomonok that operated between 1886 and 1949. The golf course was located between [[Kissena Boulevard]] and 164th Street, just to the south of Horace Harding Boulevard (now the [[Interstate 495 (New York)|Long Island Expressway]]) and to the east of [[Queens College, City University of New York|Queens College]].<ref name="forgotten">{{cite web|title=Pomonok|url=http://forgotten-ny.com/2006/01/pomonok-queens/|work=Forgotten NY|date=7 January 2006|access-date=2014-10-12|archive-date=December 6, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111206054900/http://forgotten-ny.com/2006/01/pomonok-queens/|url-status=live}}</ref> The club was established in 1886 by members of the Flushing Athletic Club in Flushing and moved to the Kissena Boulevard location in 1921. [[Devereux Emmet]] designed the golf course. The golf course hosted the [[PGA Championship]] in [[1939 PGA Championship|1939]], which [[Henry Picard]] won. The members disbanded and sold the course in 1949. Part of the site today contains the Electchester cooperative housing development, Pomonok public housing and an extension of Parsons Boulevard.<ref name="forgotten" /><ref>{{cite book |last=Quirin |first=William L. |title=America's Linksland: A Century of Long Island Golf |year=2002 |publisher=Sleeping Bear Press |location=Chelsea, MI |isbn=1-58536-087-2 |page=199}}</ref>

In 1992, New York City settled a lawsuit brought on behalf of 100,000 families who claimed that the city had steered all white families applying for public housing into Pomonok and had provided the public housing complex with higher standards of care and maintenance than those inhabited by majority Black and Hispanic families.<ref>{{cite news|author = Steven Lee Myers |title = Worlds Apart in Queens |newspaper = The New York Times |date = July 5, 1992 |url = https://www.nytimes.com/1992/07/05/nyregion/worlds-apart-in-queens.html |access-date = July 11, 2021}}</ref>

== Electchester Housing Complex ==
Electchester is a [[cooperative housing]] complex on the other side of the small neighborhood between Parsons Boulevard and 164th Street in Pomonok, which was established by [[Harry Van Arsdale, Jr.]] and Local 3 of the [[International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers]] in 1949, when Van Arsdale worked with the Joint Industry Board of the Electrical Industry to purchase {{convert|103|acre|km2}} of the former Pomonok Country Club and build apartment buildings. About 5,550 people live in about 2,500 units in 36 buildings, including a pair of 23-story towers and a network of three and six-story brick structures.<ref>[https://www.ibew.org/articles/18ElectricalWorker/EW1807/Electchester.0718.html "Off-Broadway Play Raises the Curtain on Local 3's Electchester"], [[International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers]], July 2018. Accessed January 1, 2025. "In 1949, inspired in part by a housing project for unionized garment workers, Van Arsdale proposed Local 3 build its own community of affordable, comfortable homes for electricians. One year later, the local broke ground on a site rich with irony: the former Pomonok Country Club in Flushing, Queens, where anti-union titans of business spent leisurely afternoons on the golf course. The first section of what would become 2,500 cooperative housing units in 36 brick buildings and two 23-story towers opened to residents in 1951. Local 3 purchased the 103-acre site with assistance from the Joint Industry Board of the Electrical Industry, a partnership that continues today"</ref> It is served by Public School 200, which is on land donated by Electchester. The union provided the majority of the mortgage. New York state offered tax abatements. Electchester was classified as a "limited dividend nonprofit", subject to state regulations. The first families paid $475 per room for equity shares, and carrying charges of $26 per month per room, on apartments ranging from three and a half to five and a half rooms.<ref>Harry Van Arsdale Jr.: Labor's Champion (M.E. Sharpe, 2002)</ref>

Electchester also contains the JIB Lanes Bowling Alley and a shopping center, containing a supermarket, a pharmacy and other small stores. In the early 2020’s, a [[Popeyes]] location opened in the area as well as a dental office.

Both housing complexes are patrolled by the nearby 107th Precinct of the [[New York City Police Department|New York City’s Police Department]]. There is also an NYPD PSA-9 Housing Police Unit station located in the Pomonok Houses.

== Health ==
The nearest hospitals are [[Queens Hospital Center]] and [[NewYork–Presbyterian Queens|New York–Presbyterian Hospital Queens]].

== Education ==
Nearby are major facilities such as [[Queens College|CUNY Queens College]], [[St. John's University (New York City)|St. John's University]], [[Touro College]], [[Rabbinical Seminary of America]] along with various public and private schools. The [[CUNY Law School]], formerly in the area, moved to the [[Long Island City]] neighborhood in May of 2012.

[[Queens Public Library]] has a branch in Pomonok, within the Local 3 Union Building in the Electchester complex.<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.queenslibrary.org/about-us/locations/pomonok/?filters=ev_loc:94500000 | title=Pomonok | Queens Public Library | access-date=October 17, 2019 | archive-date=May 7, 2023 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230507215834/https://www.queenslibrary.org/about-us/locations/pomonok/?filters=ev_loc:94500000 | url-status=live }}</ref>

== Community ==
Onsite of Pomonok Houses is the Pomonok Community Center (PCC), operated by [[Queens Community House]]. It hosts a senior center, after school program, and, in the summer months, a camp and teen program.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Community Centers {{!}} Queens Community House |url=https://www.qchnyc.org/communitycenters?communitycenter=pomonok |access-date=2024-05-28 |website=www.qchnyc.org |archive-date=May 28, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240528103418/https://www.qchnyc.org/communitycenters?communitycenter=pomonok |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Parry |first=Bill |date=2021-11-30 |title=Queens Community House gives away free turkeys, Timberlands ahead of Thanksgiving holiday |url=https://qns.com/2021/11/queens-community-house-gives-away-free-turkeys-timberlands-ahead-of-thanksgiving/ |access-date=2024-05-28 |website=qns.com |language=en-US |archive-date=May 28, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240528103418/https://qns.com/2021/11/queens-community-house-gives-away-free-turkeys-timberlands-ahead-of-thanksgiving/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Transportation ==

===Buses===
While there are no train lines present in Pomonok, the neighborhood is served by various [[MTA Regional Bus Operations]] routes.

Pomonok is served by the {{NYC bus link|Q25|Q64|Q65|Q74|prose=y}} routes as well as the {{NYC bus link|QM4|QM44|prose=y}} routes which run express to [[Midtown Manhattan]]. The {{NYC bus link|Q17|Q88|prose=y}} routes also serve the neighborhood on [[Horace Harding Expressway]].

The aforementioned routes and the {{NYC bus link|Q20|Q44|Q45|Q46|Q48|prose=y}} bus routes as well as the {{NYC bus link|QM1|QM5|QM6|QM7|QM8|QM31|QM35|prose=y}} express routes in neighboring [[Kew Gardens Hills, Queens|Kew Gardens Hills]] all have [[New York City Subway]] transfers and [[Long Island Rail Road]] connections in the [[Briarwood, Queens|Briarwood]], [[Downtown Flushing]], [[Elmhurst, Queens|Elmhurst]], [[Forest Hills, Queens|Forest Hills]], [[Jamaica, Queens|Jamaica]], [[Kew Gardens, Queens|Kew Gardens]] and [[Rego Park, Queens|Rego Park]] neighborhoods.<ref>{{Cite NYC bus map|Q}}</ref>

===Highways===
Alongside the [[Interstate 495 (New York)|Long Island Expressway]], the following highways are also nearby the Pomonok area:

*[[Grand Central Parkway]] at Exit 22A of the [[Interstate 495 (New York)|Long Island Expressway]] in [[Flushing Meadows-Corona Park]] and 69th Road.
*
*[[Interstate 678 (New York)|Van Wyck and Whitestone Expressway]] at Exit 22B of the [[Interstate 495 (New York)|Long Island Expressway]] in [[Flushing Meadows-Corona Park]] as well as Jewel Avenue and Park Drive East.
*
*[[Jackie Robinson Parkway]] at Exit 7A-B of the [[Interstate 678 (New York)|Van Wyck Expressway]] and at Exit 14 of the [[Grand Central Parkway]] at the [[Kew Gardens Interchange]].
